author: Trash Theory
description:
Moving into a second decade is hard for any band. Normally all the youthful energy that made them exciting in the first place has disappeared. They can continue doing what they were doing, usually with diminishing returns. Or they can break up like the Beatles did. But the key is to try something new, to evolve, to grow up. And so, entering the 90s, R.E.M. were all about change. Bored of being just kings of College Radio they set their sights further afield. No more loud electric guitars, no more mumbling, now creating songs about love and nostalgia and shiny happiness. And there was a whole lot more mandolin. The formerly cryptic Michael Stipe was now baring his soul; maybe he said too much, maybe he didn’t say enough. This is the story of R.E.M. breaking the mainstream and reshaping the 90s in their own image.
